$comment: Rules about financial arithmetic and how figures are expressed. Standards 7, 11, 12, 15, and 28. The Standard 11 rules landed first and the rest arrived with their own standards, because a rule backlinking to a standard nobody has written points at nothing — scripts/inventory.mjs refuses that. math.calc-blocks-recompute is the only rule in this catalog that recomputes rather than inspects, and the only substantive rule anywhere in the framework that may honestly claim assurance: full.
$admissionTest: Every rule here passed all five questions (ADR 0005): can it be applicable, can evidence be gathered, can its state be evaluated, can its violation be explained, can remediation change the result? Standard 11's other requirements — whether an inflation assumption is reasonable, whether a cross-period comparison's basis is the right one — fail question three and stay in the standard's prose, disclosed in its Implementation section.

rules.title: Every stated return is labelled nominal or real
rules.description: Each return, growth rate, or projected monetary figure in the analysis states whether it is expressed in nominal terms or in real, inflation-adjusted terms.
rules.rationale: An unlabelled return is ambiguous by exactly the inflation rate, and the reader has no way to recover which was meant. Over a long horizon the two differ by most of the answer.
rules.remediation: Label each figure at the point it is stated. A single global note does not disambiguate a document that mixes both, which most realistic analyses do.
rules.$assuranceNote: A lexical check. It establishes that a label is PRESENT near a figure — never that the label is CORRECT. A nominal figure labelled 'real' passes this check, and no scan available to this repository can tell the difference. Reporting a clean run as 'nominal and real are not confused here' would be exactly the false green this framework exists to prevent.

rules.title: Long-horizon projections lead with real terms
rules.description: Where the projection horizon exceeds ten years, the analysis presents its primary figures in today's purchasing power, with nominal figures secondary.
rules.rationale: A nominal figure at a thirty-year horizon reads as a far better outcome than it is, and reads that way most strongly to the audience least equipped to notice.
rules.remediation: Convert the headline figures to today's money and state the inflation assumption used. Keep the nominal figures; make them secondary.
rules.$assuranceNote: Recommended rather than required because legitimate exceptions exist: a fixed nominal liability such as a mortgage balance genuinely is a nominal quantity, and converting it obscures more than it clarifies. The checker cannot distinguish that case from an oversight, which is precisely why this warns rather than fails.

rules.title: Every stated rate carries its period and its compounding frequency
rules.description: Each interest or return rate the document states is accompanied by the period it covers and how often it compounds.
rules.rationale: A rate without a compounding frequency is not yet a quantity: 12% compounded monthly and 12% compounded annually are different numbers wearing the same label, and the gap between them widens with the horizon and with the rate.
rules.remediation: State the period and the compounding frequency beside each rate, and convert to an effective annual basis before comparing any two rates.
rules.$assuranceNote: Lexical: it establishes that a frequency is PRESENT beside the rate, never that it is CORRECT. A rate labelled "compounded monthly" that was in fact quoted as an annual equivalent passes. Whether a comparison the document draws was actually made on effective annual rates, rather than merely described as such, is not evaluable by any check this repository can run.

rules.title: A periodic payment for an amortising loan is accompanied by the lifetime interest total
rules.description: A document stating a periodic payment for an amortising loan also states the total interest paid over the full term.
rules.rationale: The payment is the figure chosen for how it reads; the lifetime total is the figure that makes a thirty-year term comparable to a fifteen-year one. Presenting only the payment makes lengthening the term look like a saving, which is the direction the error always runs.
rules.remediation: State total interest over the term beside the payment, computed in a calc block from the same rate and term the payment used.
rules.$assuranceNote: Lexical: it establishes that a lifetime total is PRESENT, never that it is CORRECT — a total computed on the wrong term or the wrong rate passes. Where the figure sits in a calc block, math.calc-blocks-recompute checks the arithmetic exactly, but that establishes only that the named function returns the stated figure from the stated inputs.

rules.title: A compounded projection states its rate, its horizon, and its compounding frequency
rules.description: A projected value produced by compounding appears with the rate, the number of periods, and the compounding frequency that produced it.
rules.rationale: A terminal value is a function of three inputs and none of them is recoverable from the output. Without all three the figure cannot be reproduced, checked, or disagreed with — it can only be believed.
rules.remediation: State all three beside the projected value, and carry the calculation in a calc block so the figure can be recomputed rather than trusted.
rules.$assuranceNote: Lexical: it establishes that the three inputs are PRESENT near the figure, never that the figure FOLLOWS from them. A projection whose stated inputs do not produce its stated output passes this check entirely — that question belongs to math.calc-blocks-recompute, and only where the document carries a calc block at all.

rules.title: An average return identifies itself as geometric or arithmetic
rules.description: A return described as an average states which average it is, and where the figure is compounded forward, it is the geometric mean.
rules.rationale: The arithmetic mean of a volatile series always exceeds the compound rate the series actually delivered, and by more as volatility rises. Compounding the arithmetic mean forward produces a terminal value the series itself would never have reached.
rules.remediation: Label the average, and use the geometric mean wherever the figure is compounded. Where both are shown, state the gap and attribute it to volatility rather than to rounding.
rules.$assuranceNote: Lexical: it establishes that a LABEL is present, never that it is CORRECT. A figure labelled "geometric mean" that was computed arithmetically passes, and no scan available to this repository can tell the difference. What is checked exactly is the framework's own arithmetic, not any document's choice of it.

rules.title: An average return states which average it is
rules.description: Every figure described as an average return names itself as arithmetic or geometric at the point it is stated.
rules.rationale: The two answer different questions — what a typical year looked like, and what the whole period actually delivered — and they diverge by more the more volatile the series. An unlabelled average is ambiguous by exactly the variance drag, in the flattering direction.
rules.remediation: Name the average where it is stated. Where the compound return is what the reader needs, give that figure and say which it is.
rules.$assuranceNote: Lexical. It establishes that a label is PRESENT, never that it is CORRECT: an arithmetic mean labelled "compound annual return" passes, and no scan available to this repository can tell the difference. Whether the gap between the two averages was then presented as a rounding difference is Standard 15 R2, kept out of the catalog because the subject is usually an absence.

rules.title: A long-horizon projected figure does not exceed the precision of its inputs
rules.description: A projected figure at a long horizon carries no more significant digits than the assumptions that produced it support.
rules.rationale: Precision reads as confidence. A thirty-year projection quoted to the cent implies a certainty that the inflation assumption alone destroys, and readers act on the digits rather than on the caveats around them.
rules.remediation: Round the projection to a precision consistent with the spread its own scenario set produces, and present that range beside it.
rules.$assuranceNote: Lexical: it counts significant digits in long-horizon figures against the precision of the stated inputs. It establishes that a suspiciously exact figure APPEARS, never what precision the assumptions actually SUPPORT — that is a domain judgement about materiality. A calc block legitimately states full precision so the figure can be verified; the prose is what this rule concerns.

rules.title: Every calc block recomputes to the figure the prose states
rules.description: Each fenced calc block in standards/ and examples/ is executed against the named export of scripts/finance.mjs with the stated literal inputs, and the result matches the stated figure within the stated tolerance.
rules.rationale: This is the only rule in the framework that recomputes rather than inspects, and it is the whole of the difference between a checked claim and an asserted one. Without it every figure in every standard is a number somebody typed, and the framework's own documents would rest on exactly the trust they tell readers not to extend.
rules.remediation: Fix the figure, the inputs, or the function — whichever is actually wrong. Never widen the tolerance to make a block pass: that is the weakening Standard 29 forbids, and it converts the strongest guarantee here into a formality.
rules.$assuranceNote: FULL, and the only substantive rule here that may honestly claim it, because it is the only one whose subject has a right answer. Full assurance is claimed for exactly one proposition: the figure stated in the prose is the figure the named function returns from the stated inputs, within the stated tolerance. It establishes NOTHING about whether the right function was chosen, whether the inputs are reasonable, or whether the tolerance suits the claim it governs — Standard 28 R6 is the statement of everything it excludes. A rule typed computational with no checker behind it would carry assurance none and report NOT_EVALUATED like anything else nothing has looked at.

rules.title: Derived monetary figures carry a calc block
rules.description: Monetary figures and projected balances the document derived, rather than quoted from a source, are accompanied by a fenced calc block that recomputes them.
rules.rationale: A derived figure with no block is a figure nobody can check, and the framework's central guarantee reaches only as far as its coverage. Every uncovered figure is a place where the arithmetic is taken on trust in a document whose whole argument is that trust is not enough.
rules.remediation: Attach a calc block naming the finance.mjs function, its literal inputs, the expected figure, and an explicit tolerance.
rules.$assuranceNote: Recommended rather than required because a figure legitimately quoted from a source is not derived and has nothing to recompute, and a checker demanding a block for every number in a document would be switched off within a week. It establishes PRESENCE and never correctness: a document satisfies it by attaching a block that computes something irrelevant, which is Standard 28 R6's failure expressed as a coverage gap rather than an arithmetic one.
